Definition: A per-page fanout skill that converts a single PDF page PNG to raw Markdown via multimodal vision.
The orchestrator that spawns pdf2md-page per page and owns post-processing, assembly, cleanup, and final manifest work.
The generic shell mode used to run pdf2md-page tasks.
Absolute path to the page PNG file; it must exist and have a .png extension.
Absolute path where the page Markdown is written; its parent directory must exist.
The positive, 1-indexed page number for the page being converted.
The positive total page count, greater than or equal to PAGE_NUM.
NONE means the skill runs in generic TASK shell mode without a profile.
The brief should omit AllowedTools because pdf2md-page has no deterministic tool dependencies or allowlist.
Raw Markdown emitted from the vision-language conversion step without post-processing, fences, or commentary.
The agent tool used to load the page PNG as multimodal input.
The agent tool used to write the Markdown output to OUTPUT_PATH.
A Markdown table format used for tables, with alignment markers matching visual alignment.
Deterministic bracketed placeholders required for visible figures, tables, and non-text images in reading order.

Synonyms: [FIGURE: <full visible caption text including the figure number>]
Definition: The required leading token and format for figure placeholders.
The required leading token and format for table placeholders.
A placeholder line written to OUTPUT_PATH when input validation or image extraction fails.
The returned status value for a pdf2md-page run.
The status returned when IMAGE_PATH is missing or not a PNG and the image-not-found placeholder is written.
The status returned when an image is blank, unreadable, or cannot be interpreted and the content-not-extractable placeholder is written.
The status returned when conversion succeeds and raw Markdown content is written.
The orchestrator-side post-processing tool run on raw per-page Markdown after fanout completes.
The orchestrator-side assembly tool that stitches per-page files into the final document.
